diagnosis: The bot is roughly break-even at the macro level (50.7% win rate, -$68.37 over 404 trades) but the loss is heavily concentrated in the MOMENTUM setup (-$55.81 over 383 trades, 49% win) and specifically in DOGE (-$23.45, 39% win) and ETH (-$25.40, 54% win but large negative tail - worst trade -$15.93 on ETH). ARB is small-sample but strongly profitable (92% win, +$5.89 over 13 trades) and underutilized. The lesson engine has already identified and is actively vetoing the 'move10-20' bucket (-$33.47 expectancy, 28/81 win) which is correctly suppressing a major leak — recent decision logs show this veto firing repeatedly and correctly. However, 'left60-120' (-$20.25, 21/59 win, validated veto) and 'price<0.45' (-$19.54, 19/62 win, validated veto) are also validated losers but it's unclear if they are being enforced as consistently as move10-20 in the live engine — recommend confirming veto enforcement parity. The 'all-agree' bucket is paradoxically a loser (-$18.99 over 112 trades, 50/112 win) despite intuitively being the highest-confidence signal, suggesting peer-agreement logic is miscalibrated or correlated with chasing already-moved prices into unfavorable entries. The bot is also trading too close to expiry in some cases (left60-120 is a validated veto but min_entry_left_sec=140 seems inconsistent with 130-150s entries that fall into the 120-150s 'good' zone — entries at 122-130s left are borderline). Stop losses are firing at steep values (e.g., stop loss @0.22, @0.19, @0.23 from 0.55-0.56 entries) suggesting stop_loss_bid=0.45 is not actually being respected as an early-exit threshold — positions are bleeding well past the configured level before triggering, indicating either slippage, confirm-tick delay, or a bug in stop logic. This is likely the single largest controllable loss driver: multiple EXIT logs show stop-outs at 0.19-0.25 bid when entries were 0.55-0.60, a loss of 0.30-0.40 per contract, far worse than the configured stop_loss_bid=0.45 would suggest if enforced promptly.
